paper.title_en: Accelerating materials discovery for room-temperature qubits via Generative Quantum Machine Learning
paper.abstract_en: The realization of stable, scalable room-temperature quantum computing is severely bottlenecked by the slow pace of materials discovery, which conventionally relies on classical Density Functional Theory (DFT) and trial-and-error synthesis. In this work, we introduce a Generative Quantum Machine Learning (GQML) framework to invert this paradigm, utilizing a 64-qubit parameterized quantum circuit to autonomously generate candidate material structures optimized for high-temperature quantum coherence. By mapping target properties directly into a quantum latent space, our model evaluated <math altimg="si190.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1144"><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> structural permutations in just 45 QPU-hours—a 99.8% reduction in screening time compared to the estimated 120,000 CPU-hours required by traditional classical methods. The GQML pipeline identified 42 highly promising solid-state spin defect candidates with predicted operational viability above 250 K. Experimental synthesis of the top-ranked candidate — a novel carbon-boron-nitride hybrid lattice — demonstrated stable qubit coherence (<math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1162"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>∗</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>3.2</mn></mrow></math> ms) at 298 K (room temperature). Furthermore, the model predicted thermodynamic stability and topological invariants with an accuracy of 94.3%. This approach establishes a scalable, data-driven pathway for the rapid discovery and manufacturing of next-generation quantum hardware. •GQML framework rapidly identifies stable room-temperature qubit materials.•Evaluated 15 million candidate structures in 45 QPU-hours via 64-qubit PQC.•Quantum generative screening reduces computational time by 99.8% versus DFT.•Pipeline identified 42 highly viable solid-state defect candidates above 250 K.•Synthesized C-BN hybrid lattice demonstrates <math altimg="si107.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1212"><msubsup><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>∗</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> = 3.2 ms coherence at 298 K.
